observations.title: Regex input originates from fixture data, not untrusted sources
observations.technical_explanation: resolveReportPath accepts reportPath values from fixture.forbiddenOutputs rules, which are developer-authored test data. The regex match and subsequent property traversal operate on the project's own ledger objects. No untrusted input reaches this code path in normal operation.

observations.title: All new Function calls execute project's own source code slices in a test file
observations.technical_explanation: All three new Function calls source their code bodies from slices of index.js read via fs.readFileSync at test time. The injected constants are hardcoded literals and the only callable argument is a trivial inline sanitizer. No untrusted or attacker-controlled data reaches any of these dynamic function constructors. This is a self-contained testing technique with no demonstrated exposure.
observations.layman_explanation: All three dynamic function calls operate on the project's own source code and hardcoded values, not external input.

observations.title: Test asserts absence of secret-rotation patterns in production source
observations.technical_explanation: Lines 17689-17694 assert that index.js does not contain rotateSecret, secret_state, withConnectionProfileSecret, or CHAT_COMPLETION_SECRET_KEYS patterns, while the adapter source does contain secret_id references. This is a security regression test ensuring the main extension code does not handle raw API secrets, which is consistent with the project's stated purpose of routing through SillyTavern's connection profiles.
observations.layman_explanation: The same test block verifies that the production source does not contain secret-rotation or secret-state handling patterns, confirming the test is exercising a security-conscious migration path.

observations.title: Test validates three distinct secret-redaction patterns
observations.technical_explanation: Lines 18463-18466 assert that the formatted diagnostic does not contain the raw secret strings and does contain redacted placeholders for Authorization headers, api_key parameters, and URL query keys. This validates that the production diagnostic formatter properly scrubs credential patterns before output, reducing the risk of accidental secret exposure in error logs.
observations.layman_explanation: The test confirms that Authorization headers, api_key parameters, and URL query-key parameters are all stripped from diagnostic messages, preventing accidental credential leakage in logs.

observations.title: All five dynamic-execution matches are test-file function isolation with project-own source
observations.technical_explanation: All five candidates are `new Function()` calls within a single test case in test-behavior.mjs. The test reads the project's own index.js source, slices out specific function bodies, and wraps them in dynamically created functions with hardcoded mock dependencies. This is a common pattern for unit-testing functions that are not separately exported. The code executed is always the project's own committed source, and all parameters are hardcoded test values. No untrusted input, network data, or user-controlled content reaches any of these Function constructors.
observations.layman_explanation: All five dynamic execution matches are in a test file that extracts functions from the project's own source code and tests them with hardcoded values. This is a legitimate testing pattern with no security risk.
